title: Best AI Call Center Software 2025: 9 Picks Updated for 2026
summary: Compare Best AI Call Center Software 2025 across AI agents vs CCaaS. See real pricing, pros/cons, and picks for every team. Start with the right fit.
body_markdown:
## TL;DR


AI call center software covers two buying decisions: autonomous voice agents that handle calls and AI-enabled CCaaS platforms that support human agents. Some CCaaS platforms offer both. This guide compares nine options for inbound and blended call centers, with best-for judgments, integration fit, pricing models, and limitations. Start with the calls you want to resolve, then decide whether you need an AI layer on your existing phone stack or a broader contact center platform.


Start with a specific inbound call flow, such as appointment scheduling or after-hours coverage. Check whether the platform can access the required systems and pass caller context to a person when automation stops.


A per-minute voice-agent fee and a per-seat CCaaS license do not buy the same thing. Voice automation may still need telephony, AI providers, integrations, and human agents for escalations; a CCaaS quote may include different AI capabilities depending on the plan.


The comparison separates voice-agent platforms from platforms that provide broader phone or contact center functions:


1. **Autonomous voice-agent platforms** for defined calls or workflow steps; check usage charges and what is included.
2. **AI-enabled CCaaS and business phone platforms** for routing and human-agent operations. Some also offer autonomous agents. Check seat licenses, AI add-ons, and usage.


Use that distinction to narrow the table below before comparing quotes. If you want a deeper dive into the broader contact center AI space, the[buyer’s guide for AI contact center solutions](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/ai-contact-center-solutions-buyers-guide) covers the evaluation framework in more detail.

## How We Evaluated


We used publicly described capabilities to develop the buying criteria below. We did not test the products or measure performance. Treat each best-for category as a suggested fit, and confirm capabilities and prices in the proposed package:


- **Call ownership.** Does AI resolve the intended inbound request, assist a human, or both?
- **Phone-stack fit.** Check routing, SIP/BYOC, dialer, CRM, and scheduling connections against your current setup.
- **Workflow and handoff.** Check tool calls, permitted actions, escalation triggers, and what context reaches the receiving agent.
- **Total cost.** Compare platform or seat charges alongside AI-provider, telephony, add-on, and transferred-call costs.
- **Operational controls.** Check test environments, call review, analytics, and exception handling.
- **Security requirements.** Ask each vendor for the agreements and safeguards required for your data.


If human agents handle most calls, compare seat-based platforms and their AI features. If AI will handle defined calls, compare usage-based voice agents. Either purchase may involve seat, usage, telephony, and transfer costs.


## AI-Native Voice Agent Platforms


Voice-agent platforms are worth evaluating when AI will handle a defined part of an inbound call. Check how each option connects to your phone stack and transfers calls to a person.


For repeatable inbound requests, such as an order-status lookup or appointment change, test whether the agent can complete the action in the source system, recognize exceptions, and transfer with context. Compare the resulting cost per resolved call with your current process rather than assuming automation is cheaper.


### 1.[SigmaMind AI](https://www.sigmamind.ai/)


**Best for:** Call centers and BPOs evaluating autonomous voice agents alongside an existing dialer or CCaaS platform.


**Pricing:**


- Pay-as-you-go:[$0.04/min voice platform fee](https://www.sigmamind.ai/pricing) , plus STT, TTS, LLM, and applicable telephony costs; no subscription or concurrency fee
- Chat agents: $0.005/AI message platform fee plus provider costs
- Enterprise: custom volume-based pricing
- Playground testing is billed as usage


**Key features:**


- No-code[Agent Builder](https://www.sigmamind.ai/agent-builder) with branching logic, API actions, variables, and escalation rules
- Model choices for speech recognition (such as Deepgram), speech generation (such as ElevenLabs), and language models (such as GPT-4o, Claude, and Gemini); confirm supported providers and costs for your configuration
- Multi-prompt workflows with node-level tool calls for CRM lookups or actions, scheduling, and escalation decisions
- Evaluate the connection method and supported actions for the proposed VICIdial, Five9, NICE, Genesys, or Asterisk-based deployment
- Test warm and cold transfers in the proposed phone and CRM setup. Verify what context reaches the receiving agent and whether a custom integration is needed.
- Ask which SIP/BYOC connection options support the proposed after-hours or peak-overflow flow and what configuration they require
- Voice and chat agents; evaluate it as an AI layer, not a replacement for a full CCaaS agent desktop or workforce-management suite
- Outbound campaigns with CSV upload, scheduling, and concurrency caps
- [Analytics](https://www.sigmamind.ai/analytics) with cost breakdowns by speech recognition, language model, speech generation, and telephony component; confirm which charges appear in your account
- Multi-client workspaces with full agent import for BPO and agency workflows
- Request documentation for any required security controls, including encryption, SSO, and private-cloud availability, and confirm what applies to your plan


**Example use case:** SigmaMind AI describes a refund workflow in its[e-commerce case study](https://www.sigmamind.ai/case-studies/ai-agent-handling-refunds-at-a-lower-cost) . Use that as a workflow example, not a forecast for your own savings or resolution rate.


**Tradeoffs:**


- Confirm where direct phone-number purchase is available. For international deployments, ask whether bringing a carrier such as Twilio or Telnyx through SIP is required and what configuration that adds.
- Modular pricing means you need to understand component costs. The[pricing calculator](https://www.sigmamind.ai/pricing) helps, but it’s not as simple as one flat rate.
- Buyers processing protected health information must verify the applicable agreement and safeguards for their SigmaMind AI plan; do not assume enterprise provisions apply to self-serve usage.
- Quality depends partly on third-party AI providers (LLM, STT, TTS), which can change pricing or performance with updates.


**Why it stands out:** SigmaMind AI is an option for call centers evaluating voice automation alongside VICIdial, Five9, NICE, or Genesys. Check which connection method, CRM actions, and transfer context its proposed configuration supports. Buyers seeking a complete CCaaS replacement should also compare routing, agent desktops, and workforce tools.


For escalations, check which call summary, intent, and customer details reach the receiving agent in your phone and CRM setup. Preserving that context can reduce the need for callers to repeat themselves. See[how warm transfers work in practice](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/warm-transfer) .


To assess fit,[build a SigmaMind AI call flow](https://dashboard.sigmamind.ai/p/signup) and check its routing, actions, and handoff in your phone stack.


### 2.[Retell AI](https://www.retellai.com/)


**Best for:** Teams building inbound voice agents that value call-transfer and appointment-booking options and can configure their own integration workflow.


**Pricing:**


- Usage-based pricing; verify the current rate and which voice, model, and telephony components it includes
- Request a quote for the proposed call volume and integration setup


**Key features:**


- Voice agents for inbound and outbound calls
- Evaluate call transfer, appointment booking, and IVR navigation against the proposed product package and your systems
- Post-call analysis; evaluate how its telephony and CRM connections fit your setup


**Evaluation question:** Test whether its transfer, appointment, and post-call outputs connect to the systems your agents already use.


**Tradeoffs:**


- A voice-agent platform is not automatically a substitute for the routing, workforce tools, and agent desktop in a full CCaaS purchase.
- Ask Retell AI what implementation work its proposed telephony, CRM, and transfer connections require.
- Compare a complete call quote, not its usage rate against another vendor’s platform-only fee.


**Cost check:** Include AI-provider charges, telephony, and human time after transfer when estimating cost per resolved call.


## CCaaS and Business Phone Platforms with AI


These products range from business phone systems to full contact center suites. Compare the routing and human-agent tools in each proposed package, then check whether its AI assists agents, handles calls autonomously, or both.


For a purchase centered on human agents, compare the required desktop and routing functions first. Price the relevant seats, AI add-ons, and usage together.


### 1.[Five9](https://www.five9.com/)


**Best for:** Established contact centers that need blended inbound and outbound operations alongside AI capabilities.


**Pricing:**


- Quote required; ask for seat licenses, AI features, integrations, and calling charges in the same proposal


**Key features:**


- Predictive and progressive dialing for outbound workflows
- Ask Five9 which Genius AI agent-assist, AI-agent, and quality-management capabilities are available in the proposed package
- Confirm whether the proposed Five9 package supports the Verint or Calabrio workforce-management integration you need
- Confirm which voice, email, chat, and social channels are included in the proposed package
- Check the required Salesforce, ServiceNow, Microsoft, Oracle, or Zendesk connector and its supported actions in the proposed package


**Tradeoffs:**


- A full CCaaS purchase can be more platform than a team needs if it only wants to automate one inbound queue.
- Verify the AI features, CRM connectors, calling charges, and contract terms included in your quote.


**Evaluation question:** Can the proposed Five9 package support your inbound routing and AI handoff without additional products or services?


### 2.[Genesys Cloud CX](https://www.genesys.com/)


**Best for:** Contact centers evaluating omnichannel routing and configurable customer journeys.


**Pricing:**


- Quote required for the selected CX package, AI usage, and integrations


**Key features:**


- Ask which virtual-agent capabilities and actions are available in the proposed Genesys Cloud CX package
- Agent Copilot with real-time recommendations
- Workforce-management capabilities; confirm which are included in the proposed Genesys Cloud CX package
- Journey orchestration across channels
- AppFoundry marketplace; check availability and requirements for the integrations you need


**Evaluation question:** Which journey-orchestration, agent-assist, and virtual-agent capabilities are included in the proposed package?


**Tradeoffs:**


- Broad journey orchestration can require more configuration than automating a single inbound use case.
- Confirm integration, AI-usage, and implementation costs in the proposed package.


If you intend to keep your existing contact center infrastructure, compare the effort of adding AI against the effort of moving those functions to Genesys Cloud CX.


### 3.[Talkdesk](https://www.talkdesk.com/)


**Best for:** Teams seeking a configurable contact center platform with call-flow design and agent-assist options.


**Pricing:**


- Quote required; verify the selected voice plan, AI capabilities, and add-ons


**Key features:**


- Talkdesk Studio: no-code visual editor for call flows
- Check whether the proposed Talkdesk package includes AI Agent Assist and which live suggestions it provides
- Talkdesk integrations; verify the specific connectors and actions required by your call flow
- Customer Experience Analytics with sentiment analysis and ML


**Tradeoffs:**


- A full contact center deployment may be unnecessary for a team automating only after-hours or overflow calls.
- Test the proposed call flows and confirm which AI and dialing features require add-ons.


### 4.[NICE CXone](https://www.nice.com/)


**Best for:** Enterprise contact centers evaluating workforce tools and AI automation together, including those with industry-specific security requirements.


**Pricing:**


- Quote required; confirm the selected seat package and AI features


**Key features:**


- Cloud platform combining customer engagement, workforce tools, and AI automation
- Check whether the proposed NICE CXone package includes Enlighten Copilot for agent assistance or Autopilot for autonomous handling
- Ask NICE CXone which security controls, audit features, and analytics are available under the proposed plan
- Compare the proposed NICE CXone suite against the contact center and workforce tools you already use


**Tradeoffs:**


- A broad enterprise suite may be more than a team needs for one inbound automation flow.
- Verify which automation, workforce, and reporting features are included in the quoted package.


**Evaluation question:** Does your team need the broader contact center and workforce suite, or an AI layer on its existing NICE environment?


### 5.[CloudTalk](https://www.cloudtalk.io/)


**Best for:** Phone-first SMB sales and support teams evaluating AI features.


**Pricing:**


- Quote required for the relevant phone plan, AI capabilities, and numbers


**Key features:**


- AI-powered conversational intelligence
- Check whether the proposed AI voice-agent package can handle the routine calls in your test flow
- Real-time analytics and automated workflows
- Multilingual call summaries; confirm supported languages for your plan
- Confirm that CloudTalk supports the phone features and integrations your workflow requires


**Tradeoffs:**


- Compare CloudTalk’s routing, workforce, and reporting options with Genesys and Five9 if you need a broader contact center suite.
- Compare its routing and reporting against your requirements before choosing it instead of a broader CCaaS suite.
- Verify that its AI voice-agent workflow supports the inbound actions and transfer context your team requires.


### 6.[Dialpad](https://www.dialpad.com/)


**Best for:** Contact centers prioritizing live agent assistance, including coaching and post-call summaries.


**Pricing:**


- Contact center quote required; do not use a business communications plan as the starting price for a contact center deployment


**Key features:**


- Real-time coaching during live calls
- Post-call summaries and tools for after-call work
- Confirm the required CRM and dialing features in the proposed contact center plan


**Tradeoffs:**


- Agent assistance is not the same purchase as resolving an inbound call autonomously; verify the latter against your intended workflow.
- Check CRM, dialing, and AI entitlements in the contact center quote.


**Evaluation question:** Have agents review sample summaries for accuracy and measure after-call work in your own queue before estimating savings.


### 7.[Aircall](https://aircall.io/)


**Best for:** SMBs adding AI capabilities to a phone system connected to their CRM or help desk.


**Pricing:**


- Quote required for the phone licenses and applicable AI capabilities


**Key features:**


- Check which routine requests the proposed AI Virtual Agents can complete. Test response timing and what context reaches a person after escalation.
- Caller intent identification and key detail gathering
- Native integrations with CRM, help desk, and business tools
- Test the Aircall interface against the daily tasks of the people who will use it


**Tradeoffs:**


- A connected business phone system is a different scope of purchase from an enterprise CCaaS suite.
- Verify that its virtual-agent actions, routing, and transfer details cover your specific inbound workflow.


## How to Choose the Right AI Call Center Software


Start with one inbound queue and a measurable resolution outcome. Then use the steps below to test product fit, integration, and the cost of exceptions.


**Step 1: Do you want AI to handle calls or assist humans?**


For order status or returns, verify that the agent can look up the order, follow your policy, and escalate exceptions. For appointment scheduling, test availability checks, changes, and confirmations. If the goal is after-hours coverage or peak overflow, test when calls enter the AI flow and how they return to a staffed queue.


For calls that require judgment or sensitive conversations, define when a human must take over. Evaluate agent-assist features if you also need a platform for those human agents.


**Step 2: What’s your existing infrastructure?**


If you already run VICIdial, Five9, NICE, or Genesys, evaluate SigmaMind AI as a possible voice-agent layer. Confirm the connection method, permitted CRM actions, and context available to the receiving agent before choosing an overlay. For a narrower comparison of agent builders, see[AI call center agent platforms](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/ai-call-center-agent-platforms) .


If you are starting without a phone stack, compare CCaaS packages for routing and agent-desktop needs. Check whether workforce tools and the AI capabilities you need are included or priced separately.


**Step 3: Per-seat or per-minute economics?**


Use the same cost assumptions for each option. Compare **total blended cost per resolved call** : AI platform and provider minutes, telephony, seat licenses, add-ons, and the human time required after transfers. Use the same call mix and resolution definition for every option.


Some requests should reach a person, so count appropriate transfers separately from failed automation. Track appropriate resolutions, unnecessary transfers, repeat calls, and the cost of each path instead of applying a universal transfer-rate target.


**Step 4: What compliance requirements apply?**


If calls involve protected health information, verify the required agreement, permitted data flows, and safeguards with **each** vendor before processing it. Do not infer that a vendor’s enterprise provisions apply to a self-serve plan. See SigmaMind AI’s[healthcare overview](https://www.sigmamind.ai/healthcare) as a starting point for questions, not a substitute for that review.


For financial services, ask how each proposed plan handles access, recordings, auditability, retention, and transfers. SigmaMind AI’s[financial-services overview](https://www.sigmamind.ai/financial-services) can inform the questions you take to its team.


## Call Quality Monitoring and Conversation Accuracy


Supervisors can score a sample of recordings for each call type against the caller’s request and the permitted workflow. Check the information used, actions completed, and context delivered on transfer. Track these outcomes alongside cost:


- **Cost per resolved call.** Include platform, provider, telephony, seat, and transferred-call costs.
- **Resolution and repeat contacts.** Check whether the requested action was completed and whether the caller needed to try again.
- **Appropriate escalations.** Review both unnecessary transfers and calls that should have reached a person sooner.
- **Call quality.** Review recordings for delays, incorrect actions, and failed integrations under realistic conditions.
- **Customer experience.** Compare feedback for the same call types before and after deployment.


Before expanding to another queue, have supervisors review failed actions, escalation context, and calls that appeared resolved but prompted a repeat contact.


## FAQ


### What is AI call center software?


AI call center software uses artificial intelligence (speech recognition, natural language processing, large language models, and text-to-speech) to either handle customer calls autonomously or assist human agents during calls. Products range from IVR tools to voice agents that may handle tasks such as refund requests and appointment scheduling when connected to the required systems. Speech recognition is one component. Compare[speech-to-text engines for contact centers](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/best-contact-center-speech-to-text-engines) if recognition accuracy is central to your evaluation.


### How much does AI call center software cost?


Costs depend on the product and call flow. CCaaS quotes may combine seat licenses, AI add-ons, and usage; voice-agent charges may include a platform fee plus speech, model, and telephony costs. SigmaMind AI lists a[$0.04/min voice platform fee](https://www.sigmamind.ai/pricing) on pay-as-you-go usage, before provider and applicable telephony charges. Compare total blended cost per resolved call, including human time after transfer.


### Can AI voice agents replace human agents entirely?


Not for every call. Define which requests AI may complete, which require a person, and what information must accompany a transfer. Test exceptions such as an order that cannot be found or an appointment the caller needs to discuss rather than change.


### What latency is acceptable for AI voice agents?


Judge response delays in the call flows you intend to deploy. Test your own call flows on the intended phone connection, including tool lookups and transfers, and review whether pauses disrupt callers or cause them to repeat themselves. Ask vendors what their latency figures include before comparing them.


### What’s the difference between AI-native voice agents and CCaaS with AI?


Voice-agent platforms such as SigmaMind AI and Retell AI focus on AI handling defined calls or workflow steps. CCaaS platforms such as Five9, Genesys, and Talkdesk provide broader contact center infrastructure and may offer both agent assistance and autonomous AI. Compare the required routing and human-agent tools as well as usage, seats, and add-ons.


### Do I need to replace my existing dialer to use AI voice agents?


Not necessarily. Evaluate SigmaMind AI’s proposed connection to VICIdial, Five9, NICE, or Genesys, including any SIP/BYOC configuration. Ask other voice-agent vendors how they would connect to your existing stack. Check your specific inbound routing, CRM actions, and human-transfer requirements before deciding whether to add an AI layer or replace a platform.


### How long does deployment take?


Routing changes, system permissions, workflow actions, security review, and testing determine the deployment timeline. Ask each vendor to scope your actual inbound flow, including exception handling and transfer to the receiving team, rather than relying on a generic deployment estimate.


### What ROI should I expect from AI call center software?


There is no reliable universal ROI figure for your queue. Establish the current cost and resolution rate for a defined call type, then compare completed actions, repeat contacts, appropriate transfers, customer feedback, and total blended cost per resolved call after rollout.


## The Bottom Line


Match the purchase to the work. For defined inbound requests on an existing phone stack, evaluate voice-agent actions and handoffs. If you also need routing and agent desktops, compare AI-enabled CCaaS packages. Test resolution and total cost before projecting savings.


Use the comparison table to shortlist products for your inbound workflow. Confirm the proposed integration, handoff, safeguards, and total cost with each vendor.
